claim: In .NET/Windows, a TimeZoneInfo Id like "Pacific Standard Time" names the whole zone including its daylight half, so BaseUtcOffset (and any offset inferred from the Id string) is wrong by one hour for the ~8 DST months — always compute conversions with tz.GetUtcOffset(theInstant) or use DateTimeOffset.
trigger: when converting timestamps using TimeZoneInfo.BaseUtcOffset or an offset parsed from the zone Id string
when a cross-host log or timestamp correlation comes back off by exactly one hour or 'no matching event in that window'
before recording a fixed UTC-offset value (e.g. '+8h') for a host in a runbook or reference doc
